title: Evolution-inspired Bayesian optimization improves enzyme variants on several objectives
summary: EvoMOBO is an active-learning, multi-objective Bayesian optimization framework for protein engineering. On steroid receptor DNA-binding domain and ParD3 antitoxin landscapes it achieved greater target-region enrichment than state-of-the-art methods while keeping sequence diversity. Applied to enzymes, it produced an old yellow enzyme variant that raised substrate conversion from 17.5% to 95% and formate oxidase variants that nearly doubled diethyl phthalate degradation in a photoenzymatic cascade, with experiments reserved for final validation.

evidence.tested: Benchmarking on complete landscapes and experimental testing of selected variants of two enzymes.
evidence.unknown: Number of variants tested and wider enzyme generality not stated in the abstract; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Bayesian optimization prioritized candidate variants without exhaustive library enumeration.
